Ghoraghorarūpā, Aghorā, Aghoramānanā, Mṛtasaṃjīvanī, Viśalyākaraṇī, Saṃjīvinī,
Jīvadhārī, Pathyā, Amṛtasampathyadā, and Rogā...

It is bright with laughter, the destroyer of all defects, bearing thousands of branches, fruits, and flowers; it is the possessor of blossoms, the remover of all diseases, free from fever, and the dispeller of fevers. It is the Veda.
She is the mother of the Vedas through knowledge, the divine maiden, the daughter who delivers [beings] from suffering;

she is the pacifier of faults and the destroyer of all defects. She is the beloved of the gods, the remover of enemies, and the cutter away of the desires of foes. [She is] glory... Oṃ Caṃ Paṃ. (Folio 53a)

She who bestows the fruits of *havya* and *kavya* offerings to the lineage of Karī and Harī; she whose true nature is inconceivable power (*śakti*); she who is the great medicinal herb of jewels and mantras; she who bestows grace through food and drink; she who is the Sky-farer (*Khecarī*), the Dweller in Keśava, and the Embodiment of Will (*Icchā*).

She who is radiant with splendor, yet appears weak; she who causes hunger, yet is the embodiment of all the gods; she who arises from the bliss of Mahādeva; she who is the enemy of worldly existence, the sovereign of the three worlds, the benefactor of all people, and the giver of well-being.
She is the form of well-being (*svasti*), yet she brings ill-fortune to those unlearned in the Vedas;
she is the purifier (*pāvamānī*), the bestower of prosperity (*svastyayinī*), the yielder of the nectar of joy (*kāmadughā*), and the bearer of the *vaha* [sacrificial vehicle].
She is the tenth lunar day (*daśamī*) and the final tenth day (*antadaśā*), the moment of union (*lagnavelā*), and she whose essence is the ancestral offering (*svadhātmikā*). May she be auspicious!
You are the sovereign mistress who, through the creation of yoga entered by yoga, brings satisfaction; you are the one who conceals the world through stillness, yet bestows birth upon it,
and whose compassion for the arising of the world is the fruit of the performance of dharma and adharma.
She is the knower of the stars, the astrologer, the all-knowing one, and the one who wears a rosary of all-encompassing wisdom.

She is the remover of debt, free from worldly conduct, compassionate toward the lowly, and devoted to the protection of those who have come for refuge and those distressed by fear. She is difficult to approach...
O Tārā, who removes the enemy of rebirth; O Śakti, who grants the desired half-attainment (of liberation); O support of the qualities such as *aṇimā*; O supportless one; O Aruṇā;
O Kalpavallī, the support for the attainment of all goals for those who are devoted.

The goddess Ilavī is the great power (*mahāśakti*) consisting of *svadhā*, who is affectionate toward her children like a nursing mother; she is to be meditated upon as the one who grants the fruit of the wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*) to her devotees, the speaker of Brahman,
and the essence of ritual bathing, austerity, and dharma.

She is the giver of Dharma, the wish-fulfilling cow who grants all desires, the eternal bliss, and the Great Intelligence; she is the support for the fruit of the half-syllable *Oṃ*, the one who liberates from the womb,
Vārāhī, the Auspicious One, the month of Pauṣa, and that which arises from the Vedas and sacrifices.
Or [she is] Nārasiṃhī, Mahāsiṃhī, Lokābdhisaptado,
Oṃ-caṃ-paṃ-pṛ0 (p. 54a), Linī, Mahākāryā, Mahārekhā, Tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrā, Mukhasvadhā, she who dwells in the center of the Meru-abode, and Sahasrāditya.

By her splendor, she causes the seven netherworlds to tremble as the tortoises supporting them are crushed by the weight of her feet; she touches the earth with her soles, causing the serpent-king’s hoods to quiver, and she is the bestower of skill upon Hiraṇyākṣa and others who dwell upon the earth.
With her face controlled by the power of her millions of mouths, she is crowded with the floods of battle against the blue enemy (Nīlavairi);
she possesses the delusion of being the white earth (Dhavaladhātrī) and Hara (Śiva), yet she is intent on the destruction of the enemies who have perished;
she is the mountain of the primordial sound (Ādri), the laughter, the flood of suffering, and the ultimate refuge for all that is to be played.
She who is not released from terrible karma, who removes the flood of non-terrible misfortunes,
who causes the destruction of the mouths of terrible enemies, who bestows the state of the terrible ones,
who possesses the forms of Brahmāṇī and Viṣṇu, and who serves the sovereignty of Indra and others.

She is difficult to perceive, transcending all characteristics, yet defined by the characteristic of reality; she resides within, abiding in the seed-syllable of the peak, established in peace, possessing the excellent color of the syllables,
and is both the reverse and the direct order of the half-mātrās of the prose and verse.
The deer, devoid of even a single color, are of the nature of the deity, consisting of the self; they are great in form yet formless, the cause of the life of all living beings,
possessing great arms, difficult to comprehend, and the destroyers of all impurities.
Śinī, compassionate, greatly delighted, the performer of all auspiciousness, the Vidyādharī of inconceivable form, the increaser of great fear,
favorable to Viśvāmitra, and non-violent toward all.
It is delightful, having the form of Nirvana, liberation, and the solitary state of final beatitude; it pacifies the poverty of devotion and destroys all calamities;
it is untainted, devoid of qualities, indefinable, and universal.

She quiets disease, she who is the boat for crossing the ocean of saṃsāra with its heat and calamities, she who removes evil, she who possesses the large eyes of a Vidyādharī, she who is like the Apsaras Gāndhārī, she whose nature is mantra, she whose nature is the sacred syllable (pada), she who is all things.
Oṃ Caṃ Paṃ Pṛ. 55a): You are auspicious, consisting of syllables, having the form of letters, the form of tastes, and the form of the elements;

you are the medicinal herbs, the knower of flavors, the possessor of movement, the follower of all the gods, the one whose form is breath, known as the belly, the auspicious one who dwells within the cage of the body.

Linī, she who is adorned with the formative forces (saṃskāra), the Mistress of the Mahāsandhyā, Kalā, Kāṣṭhā, and Kṣaṇa; she who is worshipped by Trivikrama, the Mistress of the Garden (Ārāmeśī) within the Garden (Ārāma);
Raṇamālinī, Śrīphalā, Śrīdharā, Sītā, and Śrīdharā.
Pārvatī, the daughter of Himavat, is the river of Dharma and Adharma, the mother, the one of true fame, the refuge of all beings, the bestower of prosperity, adorned with prosperity,
the remover of the heat of worldly existence, and the giver of supreme bliss; thus says the Veda.

Śakti is the one who revolves the cycle of worldly existence through the knowledge of the Vedas; she is filled with the collection of great principles and bestows the attainment of great fruits. She is the most auspicious among all that is auspicious and the fulfiller of all hopes—she is Kapilā.
Piṅgalā, Tīvrākṣī, Pravodhanā, Rasā, Mahīyasī,
Pṛthvī, Sīcā, Ekapādā, Mahāśakti, Nirañjanā, Śabdahetu,
Śabdamayī, Puṇḍarīkākṣavigrahā, and Śaṅkarā.

She who dwells in the half of Śiva, the Lord of Gaurī; she who is saluted by Rudra, Indra, and the other gods; she who reclines upon the coils of the King of Serpents; she who bestows the fruit of the supreme form of the sacrifice of the universe; she who is the destroyer.
You are the pacifier of disease, the wielder of the trident, the graceful one, the formless one who wields the trident, the moonlight, the sixteenth digit,
the ancient one, the giver of the sacrificial fee, the ultimate goal, the destroyer of obstacles, and Revatī.
Pratyaṅgirā, the most formidable, the destroyer of terrible spells and sorcery; Tripurā, who dwells at the side of Tripura and upon the Malaya mountain;
she who bestows the fruits of heaven and liberation, and who removes the grief of all sorcery.
Free from sorrow, free from fever, the fragrant earth, the universal medicine,
the supreme pacifier of all suffering, the destroyer of all diseases,
the remover of sin, the mother of the world, and the annihilator of the impurities of the Kali age— Oṃ Caṃpaṃ. (Folio 56a)
The daughter of Bhṛgu, of great fortune, the maiden of the Ṛṣis who has conquered her senses;
the embodiment of Nara and Nārāyaṇa; the Kaurava woman with fierce roots;
the mistress of life, the sustainer of life, the one who grants life and sustenance to living beings—Jīva!

The one who dwells in her own abode, the one who sustains both the living and the non-living, the knower of time, the subduer of time, the one whose speech is purposeful, the sovereign of causes, Padmā,
she who is within the interior of the white lotus, she who resides in the interior of the lotus, the thousand-eyed one.

She who causes the destruction of inexhaustible sacrifices through her speech, whose actions are meritorious, whose fragrance is merit, who serves the virtuous and bestows merit, whose limbs are variegated,
who is fair-complexioned, the daughter of Kaśyapa, the destroyer of the worlds, [went] to the ocean.
Arising from the ocean, she follows the path of both poison and nectar;

she bestows horses, elephants, and cows, bringing about great prosperity; she grants female and male servants, lordly elephants, and the like, as well as jewels and rubies—she is the Mine of Jewels (Ratnākara).
Samudrā, she who practices both dharma and adharma; Ajitā, Jitā, Puṇyā, and Guṇaiśvaryavilāsinī; Jaṭilā, Lakṣaṇā, Lakṣālatā, and Kāñcanakeśvarī; Vairocanī.
She who has been led by the Lord of the Moon (Śiva) to Śaunaka’s hermitage, the Mistress of the Lord of Crows (Kākeśvarī),
whose resolve is great wisdom, the bestower of great liberation,
complete with all auspicious marks, the refuge of all beings, and worthy of praise.
She who is worshipful by all the world, who transcends all states of existence,
the source of all actions yet unborn, the increaser of all that is auspicious,
the mother of all senses and the mind, dwelling in the hearts of all beings— she is Māyā.

She who has ascended the elephant Airāvata, the destroyer of gods and demons; she who arose from the ocean of milk, who is beloved by Kubera, the god of wealth; she who is Padmā, the beloved of the one whose abode is the lotus (Viṣṇu), who holds a lotus in her hand, and who was born from a lotus.
Gandhāpadmanetrā, Candracandramahodarī, Krauñcadā,
Oṃcaṃpaṃ Pṛthivī (pṛ0 57a), Rāvarṣiṇī, and she who bestows the fruit of all sovereignty; Siddhi, Siddhāntadūṣṭarā, Siddhā, Siddhāntasaṃhitā, and Mahāvi...

She who is vast as the stars, all-pervading in every direction at all times, the presiding deity of all prosperity, the one who encompasses everything with her supreme grace, the bestower of all accomplishments,
the most excellent mother of sons and grandsons, and the fulfiller of all aims.

The fulfillment of all desires, the destroyer of all that is undesirable, immeasurable, and beyond the range of mind and speech—this thousand names of Caṇḍikā has been proclaimed by Śiva from his own mouth. 1000. Thus ends the thousand names.
It is the cause that bestows upon men stainless enjoyment and liberation; it is worthy of praise,
the means to be accomplished, the supreme essence of all, consisting of great mantras and knowledge, the supreme bestower of wisdom, the Supreme Brahman.

She who is the very nature of the Self, directly manifest as the form of nectar, whose name is proclaimed by Śiva as "Cāmuṇḍā" and whose essence is non-duality—he who recites it, or causes it to be recited, or hears it, or causes it to be heard with devotion... [p. 57b] ...with devotion.

O Great Goddess, he shall indeed become the best of Vaiṣṇavas. On the Navarātri, at the transit of the sun (saṃkrānti), during an eclipse, and on his birth day, the mantra-expert, having offered a bali to Caṇḍikā with the root mantra, [shall empower] the practitioners.

The wise man should feed [the guests] according to the ritual procedure for the worship of the *cakra*; otherwise, by omitting the syllable *phaṭ*, he incurs the curse of Caṇḍī. A learned person should worship at the three junctions of the day, which yields infinite fruit; [by this, one attains] *aṇimā*.
O Goddess, the righteous one shall become the lord of divine powers;
having risen at midnight in an empty house, the best of practitioners should recite this Thousand Names three times through his actions.
A son shall be born to Caṇḍikā through both mind and speech.

On a Saturday or a Tuesday falling on the eighth lunar day (aṣṭamī), one should recite the *Nāmasahasraka* while worshipping a young girl with nine [offerings]; then all perfections (*siddhis*) will be held in the palm of one's hand, even without [further effort].

Oṃ Caṃ Paṃ (Pṛ. 58a). By the mere offering of food, the supreme practitioners protect themselves from hell. O Goddess, on every Tuesday, a man who performs the ritual of *lalitā* and recites this for a hundred repetitions shall behold the supreme vision in the world of the Siddhas.
O Pārvatī, one should recite it twenty times for the destruction of enemies at night;

for the sake of Lakṣmī, one hundred times; for liberation, one hundred times; for the purpose of subjugation, ten times daily; and for the purpose of killing, twenty times; and for the purpose of paralyzing, [twenty times].

Then, the supreme practitioner of mantras, the best of the seven abodes of mantras, should recite the *Nāmasāhasraka* of the Goddess thirty times for the sake of land; by reciting it once for each [name] until the end, one who has died shall attain liberation— this is not to be disclosed.

O Pārvatī, it must not be given, nor should it be spoken of, to those who lack devotion, to one who is not a devotee, to one with poor clothing, to a bad son, to one of evil nature, to one devoid of devotion to the Guru, or to one lacking initiation; by giving it to such, one becomes afflicted with leprosy.

In this world and the next, one would go to hell [if otherwise]; but by giving to a practitioner who is endowed with faith, devoted, high-souled, observant of proper conduct, and of virtuous character, one shall attain liberation. Thus [ends] the Śrī...
The *Rudrayāmala Tantra*, the *Navārṇa Caṇḍī Sahasranāma*, is complete. Oṃ. The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said:
"I shall now proclaim that [tradition] there; listen, O Kauśika."
O Goddess, the sage of great splendor declared that you are the embodiment of the power of the three worlds.
O Goddess, I grant the desired fruit to whoever recites this hymn daily with devotion; I am the ordainer of the three qualities, granting all things at all times.
Madā 2, Brahmanī, Carcikā, Caṇḍī, Gaurī,
Nārāyaṇī, Śivā, Vārāhī, Vāsinī, Durgā, Śailā, Śivā, Maheśvarī, Sāvitrī, Mahākālī, and Kālikā.
